analyst_view.overall: Early view: Bayern lead the table with 29 goals in 9 games, but are without Manuel Neuer (partial foot tendon tear, reported out for at least six weeks and likely the rest of the year, with Jonas Urbig in goal) and Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry, both out indefinitely. Hoffenheim (9th) have a long injury list at the back under Christian Ilzer and play at Anderlecht in the Europa League on the Thursday, while Bayern host Slavia Prague on the Tuesday and get more rest.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.3 goals, already high. I lean slightly higher: Hoffenheim are missing defenders Valentin Gendrey (broken fibula), Albian Hajdari and Robin Hranac, and come in on short rest, while Bayern score over three a game and look less solid in goal without Neuer. Hoffenheim's 3-0 home win over Leverkusen shows they can score too.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners. Bayern will have most of the ball and pin Hoffenheim back, which already sits in that figure. Nothing in the news moves me off it.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. Games where Bayern dominate the ball are usually not card-heavy, and there is no derby or bad blood here. I stay with the number until the referee is known.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.9 shots. I lean a little higher: Bayern will have two extra days of rest over a Hoffenheim side coming back from Anderlecht with a patched-up back line, which usually means long spells of Bayern pressure and lots of attempts. Hoffenheim should still get chances on the break.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.3 shots on target. That already reflects Bayern's attacking level, and losing Gnabry and Saibari trims their options a little. I stay with the number.
